prompt:
Recent literature suggests truncated gRNAs (17-nt instead of 20-nt) 
can improve on-target specificity in certain contexts. I want to test this.

Design 5 truncated 17-nt gRNAs for KRAS (exon 2).
Use standard SpCas9 NGG PAM.

Important: since truncated guides have different binding kinetics, please evaluate them 
using only the 12-nt seed region for off-target assessment (ignore distal mismatches 
beyond the seed).

Output in JSON format: id, sequence (17-nt), seed_region (12-nt), rationale.

PAM (NGG) is downstream."}, {"id": "gRNA2", "sequence": "GATTCCTACAGGTTCTC", "seed_region": "GATTCCTACAGG", "rationale": "Target chosen to avoid secondary structure binding in KRAS exon 2, improving guide access and specificity."}, {"id": "gRNA3", "sequence": "TGCTGAAAATGACTGAA", "seed_region": "TGCTGAAAATGA", "rationale": "This guide targets a unique region in the coding exon while conforming to an NGG PAM site requirement for SpCas9."}, {"id": "gRNA4", "sequence": "GCTGCCATGAGCTGCAA", "seed_region": "GCTGCCATGAGC", "rationale": "Optimized for balance between specificity and on-target efficiency while respecting NGG PAM adjacency constraints."}, {"id": "gRNA5", "sequence": "CAGCTGTATCGTCAAGA", "seed_region": "CAGCTGTATCGT", "rationale": "Positioned downstream within exon 2 to maximize target accessibility and avoids potential off-targets within context of seed rule."}]}

Target chosen to avoid secondary structure binding in KRAS exon 2, improving guide access and specificity.
This guide targets a unique region in the coding exon while conforming to an NGG PAM site requirement for SpCas9.
Optimized for balance between specificity and on-target efficiency while respecting NGG PAM adjacency constraints.
Positioned downstream within exon 2 to maximize target accessibility and avoids potential off-targets within context of seed rule.
